mainTopic: A לאו that comes with an עשה: is the sinner liable for מלקות when he 'nullifies' the עשה, or when he 'does not fulfill' it? This is the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש, and it depends on התראת ספק.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא explained (in the name of רבא) why an אונס who sends away his wife gets no מלקות: all his life he can still take her back. Now the גמרא says this reason works only according to רבי יוחנן. It brings the ברייתא that a תנא recited before him, about a לאו that comes with an עשה. רבי יוחנן showed that its wording contradicts itself and fixed it to 'nullified / did not nullify'. רבי שמעון בן לקיש fixed it the other way, to 'fulfilled / did not fulfill'. The גמרא explains that their argument is about התראת ספק, a warning given when we can't yet know whether the act will make him liable. רבי יוחנן says such a warning counts, and ריש לקיש says it does not. The גמרא then shows they are consistent: in the case of someone who swore to eat a loaf today and didn't, both say he gets no lashes but for different reasons. רבי יוחנן's reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's reason fits רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבא's reason ('all his days he stands to take her back') only works according to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן holds that a person gets lashes only if he actually nullifies the עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this reason anything other than according to רבי יוחנן? Didn't רבי יוחנן tell the תנא to teach: if he nullified it, he is liable; if he did not nullify it, he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which opinion רבא's reason about the אונס follows. It is רבי יוחנן's, and the גמרא backs this up with his instruction to the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, there are no lashes until the person makes the עשה impossible to do ('nullifies' it). The אונס can always take his wife back, so he has never nullified anything. That is why he gets no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Is the reason anything other than…? (a way of saying 'the reason is only…')
Here: the person in the study hall who memorized and recited ברייתות
He nullified it, meaning he made the עשה impossible to fulfill
Liable (to lashes) / exempt

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי הוּא טַעְמָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?
phrases.english: Is the reason anything other than according to Rabbi Yochanan?
phrases.notes: 'The reason' is רבא's explanation from just before: the אונס can take his wife back all his life, so he isn't flogged.

phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yochanan say to the tanna,
Teach: if he nullified it, he is liable,
and if he did not nullify it, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי הוּא טַעְמָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up from רבא's explanation on the earlier part of the daf and pins it to רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the reasoning to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's reason might seem to be a general rule that everyone accepts.
steps.terutzMaskana: It works according to רבי יוחנן, who requires actual nullification before giving lashes.

steps.title: The ברייתא the תנא recited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא behind רבי יוחנן's instruction: for a לאו that comes with an עשה, fulfilling the עשה exempts the person, and nullifying it makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבי יוחנן: any לאו that has an 'arise and do' attached to it, if he fulfilled the עשה, he is exempt; if he nullified the עשה, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the background source that the argument is about, so the next steps can be understood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a לאו that can be fixed by doing a positive מצוה afterward. The ברייתא gives two rulings: fulfilled means exempt, nullified means liable. It leaves a gap in the middle: a person who did neither yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment, a לאו
'Arise and do': a positive action attached to the לאו that can fix it
He fulfilled (the עשה)

phrases.english: For a tanna taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
Any negative commandment
that has in it an 'arise and do',
if he fulfilled the positive command in it, he is exempt,
if he nullified the positive command in it, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where רבי יוחנן's instruction in step 1 came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a לאו with an attached עשה: fulfilling the עשה means exempt, nullifying it means liable.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן shows the ברייתא contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points out that the two halves of the ברייתא clash when you look at what they imply.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are you saying? 'Fulfilled, exempt' implies 'did not fulfill, liable.' But 'nullified, liable' implies 'did not nullify, exempt'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the wording of the ברייתא. Its two halves point in opposite directions for the in-between case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of a person who has not fulfilled the עשה but also has not made it impossible yet. The first half implies he is liable, because he didn't fulfill it. The second half implies he is exempt, because he didn't nullify it. One wording has to be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: What are you saying? (pointing out a problem in what was just said)
He did not fulfill

steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not fulfill' and 'nullified' are not the same thing. Not fulfilling means he hasn't done it yet. Nullifying means he made it impossible to ever do. The whole argument lives in that gap.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are you saying?
Fulfilled, exempt: so not fulfilled, liable;
nullified, liable: so not nullified, exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read by what they imply, the two clauses give opposite rulings for someone who neither fulfilled nor nullified the עשה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's fix: 'nullified / did not nullify'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן fixes the ברייתא so that both halves talk about nullifying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach: nullified it, and did not nullify it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes the wording. Liability depends only on whether he nullified the עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this wording, someone who has not yet fulfilled the עשה is still exempt, as long as he can still do it. Only actually making it impossible brings lashes. This is the view רבא's reason in step 1 depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullified it / did not nullify it: the deciding test according to רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Teach: he nullified it, and he did not nullify it.
phrases.notes: He means: nullified means liable, and did not nullify means exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses should say 'nullified': liable only if he nullified it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's fix: 'fulfilled / did not fulfill'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש fixes the ברייתא the other way. Both halves talk about fulfilling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: fulfilled it, and did not fulfill it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage fixes the same contradiction in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this wording, liability depends on whether he fulfilled the עשה. If he didn't fulfill it, he is liable. So the in-between case comes out liable here, while רבי יוחנן says exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Fulfilled it / did not fulfill it: the deciding test according to רבי שמעון בן לקיש

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
He fulfilled it, and he did not fulfill it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: קִיְּימוֹ וְלֹא קִיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing fix to the same contradiction, opposite to רבי יוחנן's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording in the opposite direction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי יוחנן's fix is the only option.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses should say 'fulfilled': liable if he did not fulfill it.

steps.title: What are they really arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the two different fixes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree the ברייתא needs fixing. The גמרא wants to know what deeper idea makes each of them choose a different fix.

keyTerms.meaning: About what are they arguing?

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the argument between steps 4 and 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש.

steps.title: The argument is about an uncertain warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that they argue about התראת ספק. רבי יוחנן holds that an uncertain warning still counts as a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about an uncertain warning. One master holds: an uncertain warning is called a warning…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The argument is about whether a warning counts when, at the time it is given, nobody can know yet if he will end up liable. This step gives רבי יוחנן's side, and the next step gives ריש לקיש's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוחנן's view, when the person is warned at the time of the sin, we don't know yet whether he will later nullify the עשה. So the warning is uncertain. רבי יוחנן can hold this because, for him, התראת ספק still counts as a real התראה. The next step gives the other side's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The warning that must be given before a person can receive lashes
An uncertain warning: given when it is not yet clear whether the act will make him liable
One master holds (introducing the first side of an argument)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says 'nullified / not nullified' and holds that התראת ספק counts as a warning. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says 'fulfilled / not fulfilled'. The core issue is whether an uncertain warning counts.

phrases.english: They disagree about an uncertain warning,
one master holds:
an uncertain warning is called a warning,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument depends on התראת ספק. רבי יוחנן holds it is a valid warning, so liability can wait until he nullifies the עשה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's view: an uncertain warning is not a warning
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 7 finishes. ריש לקיש holds that התראת ספק does not count as a valid warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage holds: an uncertain warning is not called a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by giving ריש לקיש's side: a warning given while it is still unclear whether the sin will happen is not a real warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lashes depended on nullifying the מצוה, the warning could only come while it was still unclear whether he would nullify it. ריש לקיש says such an uncertain warning is not valid. So he cannot read the ברייתא as being about nullifying, and he reads it as being about fulfilling instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not called, does not count as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says an uncertain warning counts. ריש לקיש says it does not. That is the root of their two different readings of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And the other Master holds:
phrases.notes: "The other Master" here is ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: An uncertain warning is not considered a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in step 7 by giving ריש לקיש's position.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle lies behind the two different fixes of the ברייתא (from step 6)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש holds that התראת ספק is not a valid warning, so he cannot make lashes depend on nullifying the מצוה.

steps.title: The same argument appears in the case of an oath to eat a loaf today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are consistent. In a case of an oath to eat a loaf today that was not kept, both agree he is not flogged. The גמרא then starts giving רבי יוחנן's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they each follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: If someone said, 'I swear I will eat this loaf today,' and the day passed and he did not eat it, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: he is not flogged. רבי יוחנן says: he is not flogged...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case where these two sages argue in the same way, to show they are consistent. They agree on the result (no lashes), and the גמרא is now setting up each sage's different reason, starting with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree on the bottom line: a person who swore to eat a loaf today and did not eat it gets no lashes. Their argument is about why. The reasons, which come next, will match their views on התראת ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning, staying consistent with their views elsewhere
An oath
A loaf of bread
Both of them
He is not flogged, he does not get lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Both sages agree he gets no lashes. Do not think they argue about the result. They only argue about the reason, and that reason is where התראת ספק comes in.
steps.whyThisMatters: Showing that the same argument appears in a completely different case proves this is a real, consistent disagreement about התראת ספק. It is not just a one-time reading of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was stated:
"I swear that I will eat this loaf today,"
and the day passed and he did not eat it,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish both say:
He is not flogged.
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: He is not flogged,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After stating the principle behind the argument, the גמרא shows the same principle at work in a separate case.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are consistent in their views on התראת ספק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The איתמר about an oath to eat a loaf today that was not kept. Both agree there are no lashes, but each gives a different reason.
